core_obligations: Set up the Leray spectral sequence (proof lines 19658-19664): for an abelian torsion sheaf F on X_etale consider the Leray spectral sequence of f : X -> Spec(K), with E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Spec(K), R^q f_*F) converging to H^{p+q}_etale(X, F).
Identify the stalks of the higher direct images (proof lines 19665-19667): the stalk of R^q f_*F at the geometric point Spec(Kbar) -> Spec(K) is the cohomology of the pullback of F to X_Kbar.

Apply the vanishing (proof lines 19668-19669): by the cited theorem the pullback of F to the affine curve X_Kbar, which is again one-dimensional and affine of finite type over Kbar, has vanishing cohomology in degrees at least 2, so R^q f_*F vanishes for q at least 2.

Read off the dimension bound (statement lines 19653-19654 with the proof): with E_2^{p,q} = 0 for q at least 2 and E_2^{p,q} = 0 for p greater than cd(K), every cohomology group H^n_etale(X, F) vanishes for n greater than 1 + cd(K), which is the assertion cd(X) at most 1 + cd(K).
proof_roadmap: Take the Leray spectral sequence of X over Spec(K).
Compute its E_2 terms using the description of the stalks of the higher direct images by cohomology of the geometric fibre.
The cited vanishing theorem kills the row q at least 2, and cd(K) kills the columns p greater than cd(K).
Hence the abutment vanishes beyond 1 + cd(K).
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the cohomological dimension of a one-dimensional affine scheme of finite type over a field K by 1 + cd(K) (statement lines 19650-19655). The proof routes everything through the Leray spectral sequence of f : X -> Spec(K) (proof lines 19658-19664): its E_2 terms involve the higher direct images R^q f_*F, whose stalks are identified with the cohomology of the pullback of F to the geometric fibre X_Kbar (proof lines 19665-19667), and the cited vanishing theorem for affine curves kills the row q at least 2, leaving only columns p at most cd(K) and hence no cohomology beyond 1 + cd(K) (proof lines 19668-19669). The non-formal content is the reading of the spectral sequence's vanishing region as a dimension bound. The claim is H2: one spectral-sequence bookkeeping argument with the cited vanishing as its only input.
